newsitem.title: USA: Bulgaria grain exports seen remaining low - attache.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria grain exports seen remaining low - attache.

text.p: Grain production in Bulgaria will soar 40 pct in 1997/98 due to favorable weather and some government support but exports will remain low, a U.S. agricultural attache said in a report made public on Tuesday.

In a report prepared by the American Embassy in Sofia, Bulgaria, analysts said because of Bulgaria's barter arrangements, about 10 pct of production or 270,000 tonnes of 1997/98 wheat is already committed to be exported.
Although the government has decided to liberalize grain trade, "exports should remain low" because of high export taxes on grain to protect domestic consumers, the report said.

Bulgaria is unlikely to import wheat or corn from the United States in the 1997/98 marketing year because of increased production and availability of credit from the IMF (US$150 million) and World Bank (US$40 million) to purchase grain and other items, the report said.
"There are opportunities in 1997/98 for imports of U.S. rice due to the stable exchange rate, higher quality of U.S. rice and stable local market share of this product," the report said.

The status of the 1997/98 wheat crop in March 1997 was 96 pct good or very good, the report said. In marketing year 1996/97, Bulgaria bought wheat from Australia, United Kingdom and Poland because of price competitiveness, EU export subsidies, and lower transport costs.
American embassy attache reports are not considered official USDA data.
